Messages.Author: Henke
Messages.Body:
Does the term "additional" have to be on a card to make it stackalbe? (I.e
"...takes an additional damage..." on Thoughts Betrayed)

What happens if the same vampire plays two Slaughtering the Herd on the
vampire? Does he move two blood? If two vampires play StH on the same
vampire?

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
Henke <d98...@stud.hh.se> wrote in message
news:9ce92g$lmq$1...@taliesin.netcom.net.uk...

> Does the term "additional" have to be on a card to make it stackalbe?

No.
All cards are "stackable" or increase upon the previous effects played,
unless their card text specifically prohibits this.

> What happens if the same vampire plays two Slaughtering the Herd on the
> vampire?

"Each time that vampire takes an action, he or she moves 1 blood to this
acting
vampire when the action is announced."

Each card will have this effect, so the victim will move 2 blood to the
acting
vampire when announcing his action.

> Does he move two blood?

Yes.

>If two vampires play StH on the same vampire?

The victim would move one blood to each of its successful harassers.

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/Cardlist_S.html#Slaughtering_the_Herd

Carpe Noctem.

Lasombra

http://www.TheLasombra.com

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <20010428194202...@ng-cg1.aol.com>, Halcyan 2
<halc...@aol.com> writes

>But what happens if it only has one blood and it has two Slaughtering the Herds
>from different vampires. How do you determine which vampire it gives the blood
>to? The order the Slaughterings were placed?

There is no specific ruling for such.

Were I judging, I would simply let the affected vampire's controller
decide. This follows on from a number of situations allowing the acting
Methuselah or acting vampire's controller to order effects
simultaneously.

e.g.
4 Untap
"You may choose the order in which these effects take place"
6 Minion
"(If there are two or more such vampires, then their hunt
actions can be taken in whatever order the controller chooses.)"

[LSJ 2001-03-16]
"Subject: Re: Random Questions "
[Conflict between Day Op and Force of Will]
"The acting player can order the effects in either order."
